newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP SHARES HIT FOUR MONTH LOW EARLY MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: BHP SHARES HIT FOUR MONTH LOW EARLY MONDAY.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's slide continued in early Monday trade, with its shares dropping 28.5 cents or about 1.7 percent to an intraday low of A$16.705.
They regained some ground to be down 14 cents at A$16.85 by 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT).

The intraday low is the lowest level in nearly four months and brings the total losses since August 6 to A$1.285 per share, just over seven percent. In dollar terms the dive has carved about A$2.6 billion off the bellwether's market capitalisation.
The turmoil follows reports of cost blowouts and the resignation of three senior staff in three days late last week.
At the same time BHP flagged a cost blowout at its Pilbara hot briquetted iron (HBI) project in Western Australia.
On August 7 the division's iron ore chief Geoff Wedlock also ef John O'Connorr on August 8, with the company citing ireconcilable differences between O'Connor and the board.
BHP issued a statement unanimously confirming its support for managing director John Prescott and for the business stategies being pursued by senior management.
